asked_at: Rapido (reported on The Product Folks case library)
subject_company: Rapido (Roppen Transportation Services), same as asked_at
round_and_level: PM round, product-sense / analytical RCA; APM to PM level [uncertain]
difficulty: Medium - the metric is ambiguous (who rates whom, mean of what) and the twist is a change in who rates, not a fall in service quality, which most candidates miss
market_and_industry: India; ride-hailing / mobility (bike taxi, auto, cab). Tier-1 and Tier-2 cities, mostly mid-range Android users, multilingual (Hindi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil) captain base on budget Android phones
exact_prompt: You are a PM at Rapido. The average rider rating has dropped by 10% over the last few weeks. Investigate what happened.
source_and_verification: Reported. The Product Folks case library lists 'Rapido's rider rating has dropped by 10%' as an RCA case (https://www.theproductfolks.com/product-management-case-studies/rapido-rider-rating-has-dropped-by-10-percent), also linked from its '50+ PM case study questions' article (https://www.theproductfolks.com/product-management-blog/product-manager-case-study-interview-frameworks-50-questions). Year first reported about 2023-2024 [uncertain]. No Glassdoor/AmbitionBox verbatim found; the TPF answer is a generic checklist, so the exhibits and the root cause below are illustrative.
context_as_of: As of Nov 2026: Rapido raised about USD 240 mn in a May 2026 Series F led by Prosus, WestBridge and Accel at about a USD 3 bn post-money valuation (https://www.niftytrader.in/markets/rapido-funding-2026-240-million-3-billion/ ; https://multiples.vc/private-comps/rapido). It runs bike taxi, auto and cab, plus the Ownly food-delivery pilot. It moved captains from per-ride commission to a SaaS-style subscription / 'zero-commission' pass; captains on Reddit complained about the pass price rising from Rs 19 to Rs 50 (https://www.reddit.com/r/hyderabad/comments/1jfcyvh/). Reported scale: about 3.3 mn rides/day in mid-2025, more than half on bikes; a Mar 2026 interview figure of '17 lakh rides/day' conflicts with this and should be treated with caution (https://inc42.com/features/how-rapidos-super-app-model-is-taking-shape/). Rapido is reported to hold about 30% of the four-wheeler cab segment against Uber's about 50% and to have more monthly active Android users than Uber (about 50 mn vs 30 mn, Jul 2025) (https://www.whalesbook.com/news/English/Transportation/Rapidos-Delhi-Surge-Faces-Fierce-Competition-Driver-Grievances/6989fc94b81b2b81dc00452d). Gig unions held a nationwide six-hour log-off on 7 Feb 2026 (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/uber-ola-rapido-drivers-to-go-on-nationwide-strike-on-feb-7-what-are-their-key-demands). Rapido holds a Karnataka cab aggregator licence to Aug 2031 (https://inc42.com/buzz/rapido-bags-karnataka-cab-aggregator-licence-till-2031/). Stale-risk flags: ride volumes and Karnataka bike-taxi status change often; check before the interview.
regulatory_context: Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines 2025 (MoRTH, Jul 2025) let states permit private (non-transport) motorcycles as bike taxis, allow surge up to 2x the base fare, set cancellation penalties and require driver training, insurance and safety features (panic button, tracking) (https://upstox.com/news/business-news/latest-updates/motor-vehicle-aggregator-guidelines-2025-centre-allows-private-bikes-as-taxis-uber-rapido-welcome-move/article-177258 ; https://indianstartupnews.com/news/indian-govt-allows-ola-uber-and-rapido-to-charge-2x-of-base-fare-during-peak-hours-9457888). The guidelines also tie low driver ratings to mandatory refresher training [uncertain on the exact threshold], so the rating is a regulated quality signal, not only a product metric. State variation: Karnataka High Court halted bike taxis in 2025 pending state rules (https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/rapidos-15-lakh-riders-face-uncertainty-as-karnataka-hc-bans-bike-taxi-470779-2025-04-04); current 2026 status unconfirmed. The Code on Social Security and state gig-worker laws (Karnataka, Rajasthan, Telangana) add welfare levies and deactivation-transparency rules, which limit how hard Rapido can deactivate low-rated captains.
public_data_anchors: 1) Valuation about USD 3 bn after a USD 240 mn round, May 2026 (https://www.niftytrader.in/markets/rapido-funding-2026-240-million-3-billion/). 2) Revenue about USD 112 mn disclosed with the latest round (https://multiples.vc/private-comps/rapido, 2026). 3) About 3.3 mn rides/day, more than half on bikes, mid-2025 (https://inc42.com/features/how-rapidos-super-app-model-is-taking-shape/). 4) Karnataka: about 3.14 lakh captains and 2.04 crore registered customers across 21 cities (https://inc42.com/buzz/rapido-bags-karnataka-cab-aggregator-licence-till-2031/, date unclear). 5) Earlier Karnataka figure of about 1.5 lakh bike captains, Apr 2025 (https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/rapidos-15-lakh-riders-face-uncertainty-as-karnataka-hc-bans-bike-taxi-470779-2025-04-04). 6) Cab share about 30% vs Uber about 50% (whalesbook, 2026, secondary). 7) Nationwide strike 7 Feb 2026 (outlookbusiness). Rating values used in the case (4.62 to 4.16) are illustrative.
framework_applied: RCA framework (frameworks.md section 4: Clarify, 4 cause buckets, Hypothesise-Test-Repeat, Land it). Step 1 Clarify - metric: 'rider rating' = average stars customers give captains per rated ride, 30-day rolling, all services; time frame: drop began 3 weeks ago, stepwise not gradual; scope: about 10% (4.62 to 4.16), all cities, mostly Android. Step 2a Data/instrumentation: rating scale, event schema and dashboard logic unchanged, but the denominator (rated rides) has tripled - a population change, not a bug. Step 2b Internal: post-ride funnel (ride complete, rating prompt shown, rating submitted, stars) reveals the new mandatory rating sheet in Android v8.4; secondary check on new-captain cohort and subscription changes. Step 2c External: monsoon, Feb-style strikes, Uber/Namma Yatri moves, regulation - checked and ruled minor. Step 2d Consumer behaviour: forced raters give 'neutral' 3-4 stars, and new users from a referral push rate more harshly. Step 3 Hypothesise-test: wide questions (is it all services? all cities? is volume of ratings stable?) halve the board each turn. Step 4 Land: root cause is a mix shift from the forced prompt (about 70% of the drop), plus a real quality dip among captains onboarded in the last 60 days (about 30%); validate with like-for-like cohorts and fix with re-weighting plus targeted captain training.

clarifying_questions.q: By 'rider rating', do you mean the rating customers give captains, or the rating captains give customers?
clarifying_questions.a: The rating customers give captains after a ride, averaged across rated rides. It is the main captain-quality metric on the ops dashboard.

clarifying_questions.q: How is the average calculated - mean stars per rated ride, or per captain, and over what window?
clarifying_questions.a: Mean stars over all rated rides in a 30-day rolling window. Unrated rides are excluded.

clarifying_questions.q: Is 10% a relative drop in stars, and from what level?
clarifying_questions.a: Relative. It went from about 4.62 to about 4.16.

clarifying_questions.q: Was the drop sudden or gradual, and since when?
clarifying_questions.a: Mostly a step down that started about three weeks ago, with a slow slide continuing after that.

clarifying_questions.q: Is it across all services (bike, auto, cab) and all cities?
clarifying_questions.a: All services and all major cities, a bit worse in bike taxi. You can ask for any split.

clarifying_questions.q: Is it across platforms and app versions?
clarifying_questions.a: Android shows most of the drop. iOS is a small share of Rapido users; check it yourself if you think it matters.

clarifying_questions.q: Have ride volume, cancellations and complaint tickets moved at the same time?
clarifying_questions.a: Rides are flat to slightly up. Support tickets are up only about 4%.

clarifying_questions.q: What is the goal - fix the metric, or fix the experience the metric is meant to measure?
clarifying_questions.a: The experience. Leadership wants to know whether service actually got worse.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: You're a PM at Rapido. The average rider rating has dropped 10%. Investigate.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Before I dig in, I'd like to pin down the metric, the timing and the scope, then go through data, internal, external and user-behaviour causes in that order. First: by rider rating, do we mean the stars customers give captains, or captains give customers?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Customers rating captains. It's the main captain-quality number.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: And it's mean stars over rated rides only? Over what window, and from what level?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Mean stars over rated rides, 30-day rolling. From 4.62 to about 4.16.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: So unrated rides aren't in the denominator. That matters, because the average can move just because a different set of people rate. Was it sudden or gradual?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: A step down starting about three weeks ago, then a slower slide.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text:
A step usually means a release, a policy change or a tracking change. A slow slide could be real quality. Let me lay out the board:

Rating down 10%
|- 1. Data: scale/schema change, dashboard bug, who's in the denominator
|- 2. Internal: rating prompt UX, release bugs, matching/ETA changes, captain onboarding and pricing (subscription), support
|- 3. External: monsoon/traffic, strikes, competitor moves, MVAG 2025 or state bike-taxi rules
|- 4. Behaviour: new user mix, higher expectations, rating fatigue

First a wide question: is the number of ratings stable, or did it change?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Here's Exhibit 1. Rides are flat, but the share of rides that get rated went from 17% to 52%.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: That's the biggest clue so far. Ratings tripled while rides stayed flat, so the people rating changed. Before, the raters were mostly the delighted and the furious. If that's what happened, the extra ratings should sit in the middle of the scale. Can I see the star distribution?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 2. Fives fell from 78% to 55%. Threes and fours grew. Ones are flat at 7%.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: That fits. The 1-star share hasn't moved, which suggests truly bad rides didn't spike. The middle got filled in. Before I call it a data issue: the rating scale and dashboard are unchanged, right?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Same scale, same pipeline. Engineering checked.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Then it isn't a bug. The measurement itself is fine, but the population being measured changed. Something internal made more people rate. Was there an app release or rating-UX change three weeks ago? And does the drop split by platform?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Android v8.4 started rolling out then. It's mostly Android. Exhibit 3.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: So v8.4 replaced the dismissible card with a full-screen sheet you have to rate or skip before the next booking. On v8.4, 58% rate and the mean is 4.11. The v8.3 holdout and iOS sit at about 4.60. That's close to a natural experiment. Most of the drop comes from forcing a rating out of people who used to ignore the card, and many of them just tap 3 or 4 to get to the next booking.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: So nothing's actually wrong with service?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: I don't want to stop there. Leadership asked whether service got worse, and the slow slide after the step is unexplained. I'd measure like-for-like: take only customers who already rated voluntarily before v8.4 and see whether their ratings moved.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 4. Those customers went from 4.61 to 4.52, about 2%.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: So roughly 8 of the 10 points is mix shift and about 2 points is a real decline. Next I'd split the real part by the supply side. Did onboarding change? Rapido has been adding captains fast through the subscription and zero-commission push.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 5. Captains under 60 days now do 22% of rides, up from 12%, and their like-for-like rating fell 6%. Tags: asked for extra cash, wrong route, no pillion helmet.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: That's a real quality issue and a regulatory one, because MVAG 2025 expects trained drivers and safety compliance. Before I land this, a quick external sweep: monsoon, strikes, fare or surge changes?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 6. Dry cities dropped as much as wet ones. No strike in the window, no fare or subscription change.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: So external factors are minor. Last bucket, behaviour: are first-time customers from a recent campaign rating more harshly?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Slightly. New customers rate about 0.1 lower, a small effect.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Then here's my landing. Primary cause, about 70-80% of the drop: the v8.4 forced rating sheet changed who rates. It added a lot of lukewarm 3-4 star ratings, so the metric fell even though the service mostly didn't. Secondary cause, about 20-30%: a real decline among captains onboarded in the last 60 days, especially off-app cash demands and route issues. Minor: a new-customer mix effect. To validate: (1) the v8.3 vs v8.4 holdout gap at the same captain and city, (2) the like-for-like voluntary-rater trend, (3) low-rating tags and support tickets for under-60-day captains vs tenured ones. To fix: report a mix-adjusted rating (or rating among voluntary raters plus a 'bad-ride rate' of 1-2 stars per 1,000 rides) so the series stays comparable; keep the higher rating coverage, because it gives better signal on captains; and for new captains, add a vernacular onboarding module, a helmet and cash-demand check in the first 20 rides, and in-app reporting of off-app cash requests. To prevent a repeat: any change to rating UX ships with a holdout, and the metric definition is versioned.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Would you roll back the forced sheet?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: No. Rating 50% of rides instead of 17% gives us far more signal on captains, including the new-cohort problem we just found. I'd keep it, make 'skip' a single tap so it doesn't feel coercive, rebase the dashboard, and make sure captain incentives and deactivation thresholds use the rebased number. Otherwise good captains will be penalised for a change we made.

answer_and_recommendation: Ranked causes: (1) Measurement-population shift from the Android v8.4 full-screen rating sheet. Rated rides went from 17% to 52%, and the new raters fill in 3-4 stars, which accounts for about 70-80% of the 10% drop (illustrative). (2) A real quality decline among captains onboarded in the last 60 days (now 22% of rides): off-app cash requests, wrong routes and helmet non-compliance, about 20-30% of the drop. (3) A small new-customer harshness effect. Recommendation: keep the higher rating coverage but rebase the metric (a mix-adjusted average, plus a bad-ride rate per 1,000 rides as the operational KPI). Freeze any captain penalties or deactivations that use the raw number. Launch a new-captain quality track: vernacular video onboarding, first-20-ride monitoring, and one-tap reporting of cash demands. Risks: captains see lower ratings as unfair and churn or protest; mitigate by communicating the rebasing and grandfathering incentive thresholds. Rebased metrics can look like moving the goalposts to leadership; mitigate by showing the holdout. Closing line: 'Most of this 10% is us changing who rates, not captains getting worse. But hidden inside it is a real 6% drop among new captains. I'd fix the dashboard this week and the onboarding this month.'
counter_metrics_guardrails: Guardrails: rating coverage (% of rides rated) reported next to the mean; bad-ride rate (1-2 stars per 1,000 rides) as the like-for-like quality signal; booking conversion after the rating sheet (the forced prompt must not lower repeat-booking rate); captain churn and online hours among new captains (training must not choke supply in peak hours); safety incidents and SOS triggers per 1,000 rides; support tickets per 1,000 rides; deactivations per week, kept within MVAG/state gig-law norms so the rating isn't used unfairly. Counter-metric: customer NPS, so that rebasing doesn't hide real dissatisfaction.

follow_up_twists.twist: What if the holdout showed no difference between v8.3 and v8.4?
follow_up_twists.response: Then the mix-shift theory is dead. I'd go to the supply side next: captain tenure, the subscription-price change and city-level captain supply versus demand (ETA and pickup distance), since longer waits drag ratings down.

follow_up_twists.twist: Leadership wants the rating back above 4.5 by next month.
follow_up_twists.response: I'd push back on targeting the raw mean, because removing the prompt would 'fix' it while giving up signal. Instead I'd commit to the rebased rating and to cutting the bad-ride rate by X%, with the new-captain track as the lever.

follow_up_twists.twist: Only Bengaluru bike taxi shows a real drop.
follow_up_twists.response: I'd check Karnataka-specific factors: bike-taxi regulatory status and a possible switch to 'Bike Direct' or private-bike captains, plus local captain supply. A regulatory pause can push untrained part-timers onto the platform.

common_pitfalls: 1) Jumping to 'captains got worse' and proposing training without checking the denominator. The headline drop here is mostly a change in who rates. 2) Calling it a data bug and stopping. The pipeline is correct; what changed is the rater population, and a real quality issue still sits inside it. 3) Not clarifying 'rider rating'. At Rapido both sides rate each other, and candidates who don't ask can analyse the wrong metric. 4) Blaming monsoon or competitors without a control. The drop is equal in dry cities, and fares and subscriptions didn't change.
skills_tested: structuring, quant, prioritisation, business sense, communication, empathy (captain side), execution
